questions.question: I lived in ----- Netherlands for two years.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" with countries that have plural names or indicate a collection of states (e.g., The Netherlands, The Philippines).

questions.question: Which one is incorrect ?[]
questions.explanation: "Alps" is a mountain range, which requires "The." Use "An" only for singular nouns starting with a vowel sound.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.[]
options: A Padma is a big river.
The Padma is a big river.
questions.explanation: Use "The" before the names of rivers.

questions.question: Which one is correct ?[]
options: The Lake Chilka is in Orissa.
The Lake Chilka is in the Orissa.
Lake Chilka is in the Orissa.
questions.explanation: Generally, do not use "the" before the names of individual lakes or most states/provinces.

questions.question: ----- father in him arose to see ----- child.[]
questions.explanation: The father in him" refers to a specific quality or abstract idea within a person. "The child" refers to a specific child he is looking at.

questions.question:
At the scene, ----- mother arose in her.
Check ----- beast in you.
----- mother rose in her.
Seeing the baby ----- mother rose in her.[]
questions.explanation: the mother" refers to the specific maternal feeling/quality within the person.

questions.question: Louis ----- fourteenth was ----- benevolent king.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" with titles followed by ordinal numbers (Louis the fourteenth). Use "a" because "benevolent king" is a general description.

questions.question:
I will meet ----- man also who came here yesterday.
----- apple you ate was rotten.
----- beef we had dinner last night was excellent.
----- lunch my mother served was excellent.[]
questions.explanation: "The" is used here because the nouns (man, apple, beef, lunch) are made specific by the descriptive clauses following them (e.g., "who came here yesterday").

questions.question: This book is ----- one I was looking for.[]
questions.explanation: "The" is used for a specific "one" (the book) that the speaker was actively looking for.

questions.question: ----- big book on ----- table is for my history class.[]
questions.explanation: Both "big book" and "table" are specific items known to the speaker and listener in this context.

questions.question: I want to buy ----- piano,but I can't play ----- piano.[]
questions.explanation: Use "a" when talking about buying one unspecified item ("a piano"). Use "the" when referring to a musical instrument in the context of playing it.

questions.question:
He is playing ----- piano.
I can play ----- flute.
I can't play ----- piano.[]
questions.explanation: Always use "the" before musical instruments when you are talking about the ability to play them.

questions.question: ----- AIDS virus infection is incurable.[]
questions.explanation: Do not use articles before the names of most diseases (AIDS, Cancer, etc.).

questions.question: No article is used/needed before -----.[]
questions.explanation: Articles are used to modify nouns, not pronouns (you don't say "the he" or "a she").

questions.question: No article is used before -----.[]
questions.explanation: Articles are generally omitted before material nouns (like gold, water, silk) when used in a general sense.

questions.question:
----- water of this lake is pure.
----- water of this pond is pure.[]
questions.explanation: While material nouns usually take no article, they require "the" when they are made specific (e.g., "water of this lake").

questions.question: ----- salt tastes salty, and ----- pepper tastes hot.[]
questions.explanation: Salt and pepper are material nouns used here in a general sense; therefore, no article is needed.

questions.question: I paid ----- one taka note for ----- old paper.[]
questions.explanation: Use "a" before "one" because it starts with a consonant 'w' sound. "Paper" is an uncountable material noun here, so it takes no article.

questions.question: ----- honesty of Rahim is enviable.[]
questions.explanation: Abstract nouns (honesty) usually take no article, but "the" is required when the noun is restricted to a specific person ("honesty of Rahim").

questions.question: My neighbour is ----- photographer; let's ask him for ----- advice about colour films.[]
questions.explanation: Photographer" is a profession (singular countable), requiring "a." "Advice" is an uncountable noun and does not take "an."

questions.question: I can't forget ----- kindness with which he treated me.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" because the specific kindness is identified by the clause "with which he treated me."

questions.question: ----- Agriculture is ----- important activity in Bangladesh.[]
questions.explanation: "No article" for general subjects (Agriculture); "an" because "important" starts with a vowel sound.

questions.question: It is a pleasure to do ----- business with such ----- efficient organization.[]
questions.explanation: "No article" for "business" in a general sense; "an" because "efficient" starts with a vowel sound.

questions.question: The child likes ----- yellow of egg.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" for a specific part of something ("the yellow of egg").

questions.question: I have read ----- Rabindranath/Shakespeare.[]
questions.explanation: "No article" is used when referring to the works of an author by their name alone.

questions.question:
He reads ----- Nazrul's Agnibina. 
Rina reads ----- Homer's Illiad.[]
questions.explanation: "No article" is used before a possessive case (Nazrul's, Homer's).

questions.question: ----- telephone has had ----- enormous impact on how we communicate.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" for inventions (the telephone) and "an" for the vowel sound in "enormous."

questions.question: We have ----- breakfast at 7 A.M.[]
questions.explanation: "No article" before names of routine meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner).

questions.question: What did you eat for ----- breakfast this morning ?[]
questions.explanation: "no article" is used for routine meals.

questions.question: His fame is on ----- wane.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" in the fixed idiomatic expression "on the wane" (meaning decreasing).

questions.question: He is in ----- wrong.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" in the fixed phrase "in the wrong."

questions.question: At last the beast in him got ----- upper hand.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" in the idiomatic expression "get the upper hand."

questions.question: Always speak ----- truth and never tell ----- lie.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" with truth ("speak the truth") and "a" with lie ("tell a lie") based on standard English usage.

questions.question: He took ----- bull by ----- horns.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" for both parts of the idiom "take the bull by the horns."

questions.question: I am not in ----- know of the things.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" in the idiomatic phrase "in the know" (meaning to have inside information).

questions.question: We called him ----- fool.[]
questions.explanation: Use "a" because "fool" is a countable noun used here as a complement.

questions.question: Mr.Sen became ----- Principal of the college.[]
questions.explanation: "No article" is used before titles/posts when they follow verbs like "became" or "elected."

questions.question: Rahim went to ----- hospital as a patient.[]
questions.explanation: No article" when a place (hospital, school, prison) is visited for its primary purpose (as a patient).

questions.question: He went to ----- hospital because he had ----- heart attack.[]
questions.explanation: "No article" for the hospital (primary purpose); "a" for a medical condition (a heart attack).

questions.question: Every day ----- begins at 9 O'clock and ends at 3 O'clock.[]
questions.explanation: "No article" when referring to the institution and its routine activities ("college begins...").

questions.question: I met Lisa who is a doctor in ----- hospital.[]
questions.explanation: Use "a" because the hospital is mentioned generally; she is one of many doctors in a hospital, not necessarily a specific one already known to the listener.

questions.question: Vegetables are delivered to ----- prison twice a week.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" because the vegetables are being delivered to a specific building (secondary purpose), not because the speaker is an inmate (primary purpose).

questions.question: Mina's mother has gone to ----- school to see her.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" because the mother is visiting the building for a specific reason (to see someone), which is a secondary purpose rather than for primary education.

questions.question: ----- physicist, Gabriel Fahrenheit, invented the mercury thermometer.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" as a definite article to specify the particular physicist being named (Gabriel Fahrenheit).

questions.question: No horizon' was directed by ----- Steve Calan, only two years before his death.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the late" as a standard respectful idiom to refer to a person who has recently passed away.

questions.question: Do you prefer ----- town or ----- country ?[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" for both; "the town" and "the country" are used as general categories of environments in this context

questions.question: Draw ----- picture of ----- owl.[]
questions.explanation: Use "the" for a specific picture being requested and "an" for the vowel sound in "owl." Note: Option D ("a, an") is also grammatically common, but "the" (A) suggests a specific reference.

questions.question: I heard ----- knock on ----- door.[]
questions.explanation: Use "a" for an unspecific sound (a knock) and "the" for a specific object (the door).

questions.question: Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman Memorial Museum stands as ----- symbol not only of the greatest moments in our history but also as evidence of the darkest moment in ----- history of this land.[]
questions.explanation: Use "a" for "symbol" (one of many symbols) and "the" for "history" because it is specified by the phrase "of this land."

questions.question: One of Akbar's most vigorous opponents during his lifetime had been ----- outstanding scholar Sheikh Ahmed and, like Akbar, he was also venerated as ----- Perfect Man by his own disciples.[]
questions.explanation: Use "an" for the vowel sound in "outstanding" and "the" for "Perfect Man" as it is a specific title or idealized concept.
